about: Hand-built test vectors for classify.py. Each vector is a minimal synthetic credential with the smallest field set that should decide its case, plus the answer we intend. They pin behaviour and record decisions; they do not prove correctness, because there is no external authority to check against -- see test_classify.py's header. Every vector's `why` says what it is defending, and the ones marked REGRESSION each correspond to a bug the 2026-09-22 evaluation actually found.

vectors.name: identity -- a civil identity document
vectors.why: The base case for the largest category. Name plus birth date plus portrait and nothing else.

vectors.name: identity -- an age predicate is identity, not its own category
vectors.why: Records the 2026-09-23 collapse: age folded into identity because the distinctiveness of a proof of age is about DISCLOSURE, not about domain.

vectors.name: identity -- an address is identity, not its own category
vectors.why: Records the same collapse for residence, which was the largest single source of false positives before it.

vectors.name: org-identity -- who an organization is
vectors.why: Kept separate from identity on purpose: merging them would make one bucket 36% of the corpus and erase the person-versus-organization distinction.

vectors.name: humanness -- a real person, without saying which person
vectors.why: Kept separate from identity although it is small, because it is the near-opposite in disclosure terms.

vectors.name: financial -- an account
vectors.why: Base case.

vectors.name: qualification -- an academic award
vectors.why: Records the collapse of academic, licence and award into one category after the academic/licence boundary failed on continuing education.

vectors.name: qualification -- a professional licence
vectors.why: The other half of the same collapse: a licence and a degree land in one place by design.

vectors.name: health
vectors.why: Base case.

vectors.name: affiliation -- employment
vectors.why: Records the collapse of employment, membership and relationship into one category: all assert that a party is associated with another party.

vectors.name: affiliation -- membership
vectors.why: The other half of that collapse.

vectors.name: authority -- constrained delegation
vectors.why: Base case for the category that absorbed telecom rights, brand rights and proof of control.

vectors.name: authority -- a right to use telephone numbers
vectors.why: Records the telecom merge: a right over a controlled identifier is the same shape as a prefix licence.

vectors.name: authority -- a right to use a brand
vectors.why: Records the brand merge.

vectors.name: civil-status
vectors.why: Base case. Kept separate from identity: these are state-recorded facts about a person's status rather than attributes identifying them.

vectors.name: MULTI -- a driving licence is identity AND qualification, in that order
vectors.why: The canonical bundling case and the reason categories are never exclusive. Also pins the substrate rule: identity is demoted to last when it co-occurs, so a single-glyph rendering picks the car rather than the person.

vectors.name: MULTI -- an IBAN attestation is financial AND identity
vectors.why: The EU IBAN attestation binds an account to a natural person and carries both.

vectors.name: MULTI -- a seafarer certificate is qualification AND identity
vectors.why: Three-way bundling in the real corpus; two survive after the collapse.

vectors.name: subject: thing -- a credential about an artifact
vectors.why: A foreign-artifact affidavit gives binary data a cryptographic identity; there is no subject party.

vectors.name: subject: occurrence -- a booking
vectors.why: An occurrence is a real subject type, distinct from the party who attended it.

vectors.name: subject: evidence -- a dossier claims nothing of its own
vectors.why: The narrowed assembly rule: referencing other evidence is not enough, the payload must make no substantive claim itself.

vectors.name: REGRESSION -- edges alone do NOT make a credential evidence-about-evidence
vectors.why: The loose rule classified half the KERI corpus as assembly, because nearly every ACDC has edges. A guardianship credential names its ward by edge and is ordinary evidence about the guardian.

vectors.name: subject: apparatus -- a key-binding attestation
vectors.why: Apparatus is machinery that makes other evidence usable. This is also the vector that proved the single spine was conflating two axes: it is a self-attestation whose subject is a key.

vectors.name: subject: none -- a bearer ticket
vectors.why: Possession is the whole binding; there is no subject at all. Requires POSITIVE bearer vocabulary, so that the bucket cannot act as a residual.

vectors.name: alignment: self-attested -- party attributes with no issuee
vectors.why: A credential with no issuee may still be about a party: its issuer.

vectors.name: REGRESSION -- no field list must NOT default to ordinary
vectors.why: The single worst defect found: 19 of 42 misses came from one rule that rendered wallet attestations, device credentials and a relying party's own registration certificate as evidence about the person presenting them. Silent, confident and in the one direction that matters.

vectors.name: REGRESSION -- a declared issuee outranks object vocabulary
vectors.why: Two bugs in one vector. `be` (proof-of-control's bits of entropy in the challenge) was matching the apparatus vocabulary and classifying a credential about a person as machinery. And `res` made the same credential look like a credential about a resource -- but a proof of control is about the PARTY who controls the thing, not about the thing. An object in the payload is what the claim is made WITH. Note the empty category list: `control` folded into `authority` at the collapse and has no field vocabulary yet, which is a known gap rather than an intended answer.

vectors.name: REGRESSION -- `issuing_organization` names the issuer, not an org the credential is about
vectors.why: It appears in the EU IBAN and MSISDN attestations, which are about individuals, and was tagging both org-identity.

vectors.name: REGRESSION -- a biometric template in an mDL is not a humanness claim
vectors.why: `biometric_template_xx` is an identity element. Humanness means an assertion that the holder is a real person, which is a different claim from a biometric being on file.

vectors.name: REGRESSION -- a citation is about external content, so its subject is a thing
vectors.why: Written first as `occurrence`, which was wrong and was copied from what the classifier happened to do: `sdt` (snapshot date) sat in the occurrence vocabulary. A citation points at non-ACDC content with a digest and a content type, which is the same shape as a foreign-artifact affidavit, so `thing` is the consistent answer. This vector is the reason the suite is worth having: it caught an expectation that had been written from observed behaviour instead of from intent.

vectors.name: financial -- an account with no money is not financial
vectors.why: Daniel, 2026-09-24: a bare `account` is just as likely a user account, or a witness's account of events, as a bank account. With no floating-point field and no currency code or symbol anywhere, it is not money. Found when the accident bundle's witness statements rendered with a banknote.

values.account: The northbound car entered the junction on amber.

vectors.name: financial -- an account beside a currency code is financial
vectors.why: The other half of the same ruling: `account` counts as money when the credential also carries a currency, here an ISO 4217 code in a disclosed value.

vectors.name: financial -- an account beside a floating-point field is financial
vectors.why: The ruling's other form of evidence: a field whose declared JSON Schema type is `number`.

vectors.name: affiliation -- an organization identifier beside a role names where the role is held
vectors.why: Daniel, 2026-09-24, on the vLEI Engagement Context Role credential: 'It is asserting that a person has a particular role at a given org.' The LEI names the organization the role is at, so a bare org identifier beside a role field is not evidence of org-identity. An org's legal name or registration detail still would be.

vectors.name: authority -- the title names an authorization
vectors.why: Daniel, 2026-09-24: 'can't you get authority from the authorization credential because it has authorization in its name?' The vLEI ECR Authorization credential carries exactly the fields of the ECR credential it authorizes, so only its title says what it is. A category the title names is also placed first, because the title says what the credential is for.
